item.title: In 1958, 58 pigs were removed from Clipperton, helping seabirds grow to 137,000
item.description: Feral pigs introduced to Clipperton Island devastated seabird populations and land crabs. Ornithologist Kenneth Stager removed fifty-eight pigs, allowing the ecosystem to gradually recover. This removal helped the seabird colony grow from 650 to over 137,000 birds. Later, black rats arrived, impacting the island's vegetation and bird populations negatively. Clipperton's story highlights invasive species' profound ecological effects on islands.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: The ground beneath Poland's wind turbines became nesting grounds for wild bees
item.description: In Poland, the bases of wind turbines have emerged as surprising havens for pollinators. Research highlights that these zones foster a thriving community of wild bees and a variety of plant species. The bare gravel and low maintenance create perfect nesting sites for ground-nesting bees. While butterflies opt for grasslands, both flies and grasslands flourish equally in these overlooked yet vital habitats for biodiversity on farmland.

item.title: China's new solar plant made with 15,927 mirrors will power 50,000 homes while saving 60,000 tons of coal annually
item.description: China has proudly completed the construction of the world's tallest solar thermal power plant at an impressive altitude of over 15,000 feet. Known as the Tushuo facility, this 100 MW powerhouse utilizes mirrors to effectively concentrate solar energy onto molten salts. The resulting stored heat will generate electricity even after sunset, ultimately supplying power to approximately 50,000 households each year once connected to the grid.

item.title: Minnesota teen builds system that cut seizure recurrence by 70.1% in worms
item.description: Evan Morris created a low-cost system using worms and ultrasound. This system helps study seizure suppression and reduces recurrence by seventy percent. The project utilizes sonogenetics and a computer-controlled closed-loop detection method. Morris received a significant award for his innovative life science research. His work offers a faster, less expensive platform for neuroscience exploration.

item.title: Archaeologists find young woman buried with fetus in a Swedish cave; remains may be up to 9,500 years old
item.description: In a remarkable archaeological find, researchers uncovered the ancient remains of a pregnant woman along with her fetus in a Swedish cave. Dating back approximately 8,000 to 9,500 years, this discovery ranks among the earliest known burials of pregnant women. Future investigations will involve DNA analysis and radiocarbon dating to gain further insights. The cave is likely to have been used for the burial of other individuals as well.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: 'Begin discussions': South Korea's Lee Jae Myung calls for talks with North Korea
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung seeks peace talks to formally end the Korean War. He also wants to discuss North Korea's nuclear capabilities and reduce regional tensions. This proposal comes as North Korea strengthens its military ties with Russia. Annual US-South Korean military exercises are scheduled to begin soon. Lee also addressed improving relations with Japan and fostering prosperity.

item.title: Michigan shooting: 5 killed, 1 critically injured, gunman found dead after manhunt
item.description: Five people died in a northern Michigan shooting on Friday. The suspected gunman was later found dead after a large search. One other person sustained critical injuries and was hospitalized. Investigators discovered a fourth victim at another residence during the extensive search. The circumstances surrounding the deaths and the motive remain under investigation.

item.title: A Cape Cod couple moved into their newly built dream home in March 2025
item.description: In Massachusetts, a newly built residence was taken by state officials for a bridge project, much to the dismay of the Hendel couple who relocated there only a month prior. This eminent domain decision affects thirteen properties in Round Hill as the state prepares for Sagamore Bridge's replacement, causing distress over disrupted retirement plans and unsettled financial futures.

item.title: A Welsh family lost Menna Owen at 18 after a cardiac arrest; her heart and lungs were...
item.description: In recent times, there has been a notable drop in family consent rates for organ donation in the UK, resulting in an unprecedented number of patients on transplant waiting lists. To combat this issue, NHS Blood and Transplant has initiated a campaign aimed at boosting registration among potential donors. Menna Owen's experience serves as a poignant reminder that having clear donation preferences can provide solace and ultimately save lives.

item.title: Europe is racing to eradicate a crayfish that can reproduce without mating; in the Czech Republic...
item.description: European conservationists are launching a campaign to eradicate new populations of marbled crayfish, notorious for their rapid reproduction and the deadly diseases they carry. Funded by the European Union, these swift action initiatives aim to tackle invasive species promptly, mitigating the risk of extensive environmental and economic harm while safeguarding native ecosystems from foreign invaders.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Berlin swimming pool cancels ‘Black communities only’ event over security concerns after backlash
item.description: Berlin’s Volksbuhne swimming pool has cancelled a planned event exclusively for Black communities after facing backlash over restricted access. The €300,000 temporary pool was due to close to the general public for six hours on August 14. Organisers cited security concerns, saying Black children and teenagers had faced right-wing and racist harassment at swimming events.
